Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G1635; unwilling:--against the will.
BiblicalUsage: Once only. Paul says if he preaches against his will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto him — the work is his whether he likes it or not.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for unwilling carries little weight on its own; its weight is Paul's point, that the gospel was committed to him whether he felt like it or not — the calling stands whether the willingness does.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
